editorial.headline: Cement and Construction Materials: Nationally Open, Bali Closed to PMA
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity spans cement, lime, sand and stone materials; it is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but cannot be registered by PMA in Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity through PMA in Bali today. That is the central fact behind an otherwise broad wholesale category covering essential construction materials: cement, lime, sand, gravel, stone, crushed stone, stone slabs, marble and mosaic cubes. The scope also specifically includes white and grey Portland cement, lime-pozzolan cement, Portland-pozzolan cement, quicklime and building lime. In practical terms, this is the commercial trade of materials that move through the construction supply chain, rather than the construction work itself.

The activity is open to businesses at **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah,** and **Besar** scale. Its breadth matters. A company registered here may operate around a varied materials catalogue, from bulk cement and sand to gravel, decorative stone, marble and mosaic elements, provided its work remains within wholesale trade. The category is therefore defined by the movement of these construction inputs through commerce, with both basic building materials and more finished stone products appearing within the stated scope.

Nationally, the position is straightforward: the activity is **TERBUKA** to foreign investment, with a maximum foreign ownership level of **100%**. The national reference given is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali changes the operating picture decisively. The record classifies the Bali position as **BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO** because, at the **Besar** scale, OSS risk is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every stated scope. Bali’s province-wide, permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, and the record ties this outcome to the moratorium of 13 May 2026.

That distinction should be read plainly rather than softened into a technical footnote. Full foreign ownership is available at the national level, yet Bali’s PMA registration route is blocked for this activity. For founders, the question is not whether the materials themselves fall outside the category—they are expressly included—but whether the proposed place of registration is compatible with the applicable investment route. On this record, Bali is not.
editorial.pullQuote: Full foreign ownership is available nationally, yet Bali’s PMA registration route is blocked for this activity.
